name: 5 Rivers NRM Community Onground Works Projects
summary: Funding for landcare and bushcare works in the Peel-Harvey Catchment of Western Australia, such as fencing, weed and feral animal control and revegetation, for landholders and community groups.

steps: Application completed with a 5 Rivers NRM officer

eligibility.rule: Project addresses at least one listed funding priority
Proposed works are technically feasible and meet or exceed the minimum standards
Activities have not already been undertaken or commenced
Activities have no potential to harm nationally or locally important natural assets
Activities are not a statutory responsibility or development approval condition
Activities are not business, commercial or predominantly private-benefit activities

documents: Quotes for each material or eligible activity seeking funding

applicant_types.quote: Funding is available for eligible landholders and community groups in the Peel-Harvey Catchment for landcare and bushcare works including:

geography.quote: Funding is available for eligible landholders and community groups in the Peel-Harvey Catchment for landcare and bushcare works including:

access.quote: Interested? Contact us at 5 Rivers NRM to discuss your project ideas and eligibility against funding priorities

effort.quote: These Guidelines are to assist landholders, community groups, schools and local governments who have submitted EOI’s for on-ground projects
Round 1 completed applications are due on Friday 4th September 2026.
Applications will be assessed against the selection criteria by our Panel who make recommendations for approval.

eligibility.quote: Project proposals must address one or more of these priorities and ensure that they comply with all requirements included in these Guidelines.
Ensure proposed works are technically feasible and will meet or exceed Minimum Standards (See Appendix 1)
Activities that have already been undertaken or commenced (there is no retrospective funding).
Activities that do not have an on-ground emphasis.
Activities with the potential to adversely impact on any Matter of National Environmental Significance as identified under the EPBC Act or any other locally or regionally important natural assets.

Activities that are considered a statutory responsibility of governments or of private land managers, such as standard boundary fencing, or that are a condition of any kind of development approval (including building licences and subdivision approvals).
Business development activities, commercial activities or activities considered to be predominately of private benefit.

after_award.quote: A completed and signed final project report and acquittal statement.
following a site visit by a 5 Rivers NRM officer

documents.quote: Quotes are required for each of the materials (or other eligible activities) for which you are seeking funding.
